answer: To resist sybils, admission is a slow, rivalrous process, not a key-generation event. An applicant locks a bond and keeps it immobile while non-kin-attested work accumulates, the way basalt becomes a foundation only after cooling under pressure. Grade and vote rights then accrue solely along a vine of those attestations; a clone starts with no edges and cannot borrow another's path. Each applicant must also publish a unique sonnet, hashed into the bond; reused or templated wording collides on-ledger and slashes the stake, so farms cannot stamp one essay onto thousands of keys.
